facts.statement: Vouivria was a herbivorous sauropod dinosaur belonging to the family Brachiosauridae that lived in what is now France during the Late Jurassic.
facts.quote: Vouivria is a genus of herbivorous sauropod dinosaur, belonging to the Brachiosauridae, that lived in the area of present France during the Late Jurassic.

facts.statement: Workers discovered large fossil bones at a chalkstone quarry near Damparis, France, in April 1934.
facts.quote: In April 1934, workers noticed the presence of large fossil bones in the southeastern face of the quarry.

facts.statement: The excavation of the Vouivria skeleton began in May 1934 and concluded on June 22, 1934.
facts.quote: The excavation started in May and was finished on 22 June 1934.

facts.statement: The genus Vouivria and its type species V. damparisensis were formally named and described in 2017 by Philip D. Mannion, Ronan Allain, and Olivier Moine.
facts.quote: In 2017, Philip D. Mannion, Ronan Allain and Olivier Moine named and described the type species Vouivria damparisensis.

facts.statement: Vouivria lived approximately 163.5 to 157.3 million years ago during the Oxfordian stage of the Late Jurassic.
facts.quote: Its age is likely between 163.5 and 157.3 million years.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen of Vouivria is a partial skeleton that lacks the skull.
facts.quote: It consists of a partial skeleton lacking the skull.

facts.statement: The skeleton includes numerous elements such as neck and back vertebrae, ribs, shoulder blades, forelimb bones, pelvic bones, and leg bones, but excludes the skull.
facts.quote: It contains five teeth, three neck vertebrae, two back vertebrae, the first four vertebrae of the sacrum, a front tail vertebra, ribs, both shoulderblades, the right coracoid, the right humerus, both ulnae, a right carpal, the first, second and third right metacarpals, the first phalanges of the first to fourth left fingers, two possible hand claws, the left pelvis, the right ischium, both thighbones, both shinbones, both calfbones, a left astragalus, the first left metatarsal and the first, second and third right metatarsals.

facts.statement: Vouivria is estimated to have reached a body length of fifteen meters and a weight of fifteen tonnes.
facts.quote: The body length of Vouivria has been estimated at fifteen metres, its weight at fifteen tonnes.

facts.statement: The femur (thighbone) of Vouivria measures 146 centimeters in length.
facts.quote: The thighbone length is 146 centimetres.

facts.statement: The third metacarpal of Vouivria features a unique ridge that splits into a bulge near the top quarter of the bone when held vertically.
facts.quote: In the third metacarpal of the hand, the ridge that runs along the inner rear corner of the shaft, if the bone is held vertically, splits at about a quarter of the shaft length measured from the top, the outer branch having the form of a bulge.

facts.statement: The fourth metacarpal of Vouivria possesses a flange along the top third of its inner rear corner.
facts.quote: The fourth metacarpal has a flange along the top third of the inner rear corner.

facts.statement: Two transverse ridges run between the lower condyles of the Vouivria femur at the border with the rear shaft.
facts.quote: Between the lower condyles of the thighbone, two transverse ridges run, at the border with the rear shaft.

facts.statement: Well-formed laminae on the front underside and rear underside of the transverse process distinguish the front tail vertebrae of Vouivria from its closest relatives.
facts.quote: In the front tail vertebrae both the anterior centrodiapophyseal lamina (ACDL) and the posterior centrodiapophyseal lamina (PCDL), ridges that run on the front underside, respectively the rear underside, of the transverse process towards the vertebral body, are well-formed.

facts.statement: The humerus of Vouivria has a deltopectoral crest that doubles in transverse width as it extends downward.
facts.quote: The humerus or upper arm bone, has a deltopectoral crest, serving for the attachment of the deltoid muscle and the pectoralis major, that doubles in transverse width to below.

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analysis places Vouivria as a basal member of the Brachiosauridae, positioned between Europasaurus and Brachiosaurus altithorax.
facts.quote: This was confirmed by a phylogenetic analysis in 2017, showing Vouivria to be a basal member of the Brachiosauridae, placed above Europasaurus and below Brachiosaurus altithorax in the evolutionary tree.

facts.statement: The genus name Vouivria is derived from a French legend of a winged dragon or wyvern known as 'la vouivre'.
facts.quote: The generic name is a latinisation of French la vouivre — itself derived from Latin vipera, "adder" — a winged dragon or wyvern from local legend.

facts.statement: Evidence suggests Vouivria died near a coastal lagoon, was scavenged by theropods, and was subsequently buried by a new chalk layer that preserved its bones.
facts.quote: From this it was concluded in 2017 that the animal had died in situ near a coastal lagoon, its weight forming a lens in soft chalkstone, and after an exposure of several years during which it was scavenged by theropods, was covered by a new chalk layer which protected the bones after hardening.

facts.statement: Workers discovered large fossilized bones in a chalk quarry in April 1934.
facts.quote: En abril de 1934, los obreros notaron la presencia de grandes huesos fosilizados en la cara sureste de la cantera.

facts.statement: The excavation of the fossil site began in May and ended on June 22, 1934.
facts.quote: La excavación inició en mayo y finalizó el 22 de junio de 1934.

facts.statement: Philip D. Mannion, Ronan Allain, and Olivier Moine named and described the type species Vouivria damparisensis in 2017.
facts.quote: En 2017, Philip D. Mannion, Ronan Allain y Olivier Moine nombraron y describieron a la especie tipo Vouivria damparisensis.

facts.statement: The genus name Vouivria is a Latinization of the French word vouivre, derived from the Latin vipera (viper), referring to a winged dragon or wyvern from local legend.
facts.quote: El nombre del género es una latinización del francés la vouivre, el cual a su vez deriva del latín vipera, "víbora", un dragón alado o wyvern de una leyenda local.

facts.statement: The species name damparisensis refers to the animal's origin in Damparis.
facts.quote: El nombre de la especie se refiere a su procedencia de Damparis.

facts.statement: The holotype was found in the Calcaires de Clerval formation, likely in the Tidalites member of Mouchard, dating to the middle to late Oxfordian stage.
facts.quote: El holotipo, MNHN.F.1934.6 DAM 1-42, fue hallado en una capa de la formación Calcaires de Clerval, posiblemente en el miembro Tidalites de Mouchard el cual data de mediados a finales de la época del Oxfordiense.

facts.statement: The animal likely lived between 163.5 and 157.3 million years ago.
facts.quote: Su edad probablemente va de 163.5 a 157.3 millones de años.

facts.statement: The bones were recovered from a surface area of approximately thirty square meters.
facts.quote: Los huesos fueron recuperados en un área de superficie de alrededor de treinta metros cuadrados.

facts.statement: Researchers concluded in 2017 that the animal died in situ near a coastal lagoon, its weight formed a slump in soft chalk, it was exposed for years while being partially consumed by theropods, and was finally protected by a new layer of hardened chalk.
facts.quote: De este detalle se concluyó en 2017 que el animal había muerto in situ cerca de una laguna costera, mientras su peso formó un lentejón en la tiza blanda, y tras haber quedado expuesto durante varios años durante los cuales fue consumido por terópodos, quedó cubierto por una nueva capa de tiza la cual protegió a los huesos tras endurecerse.

facts.statement: The fossil consists of a partial skeleton that lacks a skull.
facts.quote: Consiste de un esqueleto parcial el cual carece de cráneo.

facts.statement: The skeleton includes five teeth, three cervical vertebrae, two dorsal vertebrae, the first four sacral vertebrae, a front tail vertebra, ribs, both scapulae, the right coracoid, right humerus, both ulnae, a right carpus, the first three metacarpals, the first four proximal phalanges of the left hand, two possible manual claws, the left pelvis, right ischium, both femurs, both tibiae, both fibulae, a left astragalus, the left first metatarsal, and the right first three metatarsals.
facts.quote: Incluye cinco dientes, tres vértebras del cuello, dos vértebras dorsales, las primeras cuatro vértebras del sacro, una vértebra frontal de la cola, costillas, ambas escápulas, el coracoides derecho, el húmero derecho, ambos cúbitos, un carpo derecho, el primer, segundo y tercer metacarpos, las primeras falanges de los dedos primero al cuarto en la mano izquierda, dos posibles garras manuales, la pelvis izquierda, el isquion derecho, ambos fémures, ambas tibias, ambos peronés, un astrágalo izquierdo, el primer metatarso izquierdo y el primer, segundo y tercer metatarsos derechos.

facts.statement: Albert-Félix de Lapparent originally considered the specimen to belong to the family Brachiosauridae.
facts.quote: Ya en su momento de Lapparent consideró que el espécimen pertenecía a la familia de los braquiosáuridos.

facts.statement: A 2017 phylogenetic analysis confirmed that Vouivria is a basal member of Brachiosauridae, positioned above Europasaurus and below Brachiosaurus altithorax on the evolutionary tree.
facts.quote: Esto fue confirmado por un análisis filogenético en 2017, mostrando que Vouivria es un miembro basal de este grupo, situándose por encima de Europasaurus y debajo de Brachiosaurus altithorax en el árbol evolutivo.

facts.statement: If correct, Vouivria could be the oldest known brachiosaurid and the oldest member of the Titanosauriformes.
facts.quote: De ser correcto, esto podría hacer a Vouivria el más antiguo braquiosáurido conocido y el miembro más antiguo de los Titanosauriformes.

facts.statement: Seven theropod teeth found among the bones were assigned to Megalosaurus insignis.
facts.quote: Siete dientes de terópodo hallados entre los huesos fueron asignados a Megalosaurus insignis.

rejected.quote: In the middle and rear neck vertebrae, the spinopostzygapophyseal laminae, or SPOLs, ridges that run from the rear joint processes to the neural spine, thicken towards the rear near the top of the spine.
